en: The Noble Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra in Fifty Verses, spoken by the Buddha.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, Imperial Censor and Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial,
Dharma-Master Subject Shi Hu, by imperial decree.
Thus have I heard:

At one time the Buddha was staying on Vulture Peak Mountain near the city of Rājagṛha, together with a great assembly of one thousand two hundred and fifty bhikṣus. All of them were arhats whose outflows were exhausted and who were free from further afflictions;
their minds were well-liberated and they had attained penetrating wisdom.
Like a great nāga king, he has severed all fetters of existence, laid down the heavy burden,
accomplished what was to be done, attained his own benefit, and his mind has attained mastery. At that time,
the Buddha addressed the Venerable Subhūti:

"If there are good men or good women, as well as śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, who delight in practicing and studying for unexcelled bodhi, you people, by hearing, receiving, reading, reciting, and explaining this Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra in detail, shall swiftly attain perfect enlightenment."

“Subhūti! This Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra is fully endowed with skillful means and penetrates the profound Dharma-treasury of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas; you should study it and practice it in this manner.”

“Subhūti! If there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, regarding this Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, rejoice in it, hear it, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, they should train in this way and practice in this way.”
Why is this? Because this sutra extensively expounds the profound treasury of the Dharma of the *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas. "Subhūti!..."

Furthermore, within this Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, all the dharmas of the śrāvakas, the dharmas of the pratyekabuddhas, the dharmas of the bodhisattvas, and the factors of enlightenment, as well as all the dharmas of all Buddhas and all the dharmas of the Prajñāpāramitā, are gathered and subsumed, being equal and one.
At that time, Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

How is it that all the dharmas of the śrāvakas, the dharmas of the pratyekabuddhas, the dharmas of the bodhisattvas, the factors of enlightenment, as well as all the dharmas of all Buddhas and all the prajñāpāramitās, when gathered and subsumed together, are equal and one?”
The Buddha told Subhūti: "All the perfection of giving, the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of patience,
the perfection of diligence, the perfection of meditative concentration, and the perfection of wisdom— internally..."
Emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, great emptiness, emptiness of the ultimate truth, emptiness of the conditioned, emptiness of the unconditioned,
emptiness of non-alteration, emptiness of the signless, emptiness of self-characteristic, emptiness of the limit of existence,
emptiness of the limit of non-existence, emptiness of nature, emptiness of intrinsic nature, emptiness of non-nature, and emptiness of self-nature.
The emptiness of the self-nature of non-existence, the emptiness of all phenomena, the four foundations of mindfulness,
the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening,
the eightfold noble path, the four noble truths, the four formless attainments, the eight liberations, the nine sequential dharmas, the gateways to liberation of emptiness, and signlessness.
The gate of liberation, the gate of wishless liberation, all gates of samādhi and dhāraṇī, the four wisdoms, the five supernormal powers,
the ten powers of all Tathāgatas, the four fearlessnesses, great loving-kindness, great compassion,
the eighteen unique qualities, and the fruits of srotāpanna, sakṛdāgāmin, and [anāgāmin]...
The fruit of the Anāgāmin, the fruit of the Arhat, the fruit of the Pratyekabuddha, and the bodhisattva’s knowledge of all paths—
all such wholesome dharmas and all *prajñāpāramitās* are gathered together and equally embraced, as one and without distinction.
At that time, having heard what the Buddha had spoken, Subhūti addressed the World-Honored One, saying:

"This present sutra gathers and encompasses all wholesome dharmas and all *prajñāpāramitās*. It is equal and uniform, profoundly deep and subtle, with an intention that is far-reaching, difficult to understand, and difficult to know."
The Buddha said: “Subhūti, it is so, it is so!”
"It is as you have said, Subhūti!

Those who have not planted roots of goodness, who associate with evil friends, who are of dull faculties, indolent, ignorant, and foolish; those with little understanding and little learning, who are beginners of shallow insight, and those who delight in the Hīnayāna and possess narrow and inferior wisdom—these will find this Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra difficult to understand and difficult to enter, and they will not believe or accept it."
"You all should know this. Furthermore, Subhūti,

if there are sons of good family or daughters of good family who, regarding this Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, rejoice in it, listen to it, receive it, read it, recite it, and expound it, they will, like those who uphold the Buddhas of the past, future, and present, before long swiftly attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."

When the Buddha had finished preaching this sutra, the Venerable Subhūti, along with all the bodhisattvas, devas, humans, asuras, and others, having heard what the Buddha taught, were all greatly rejoiced; they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
The Noble Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra in Fifty Verses Spoken by the Buddha
